# dev-cli

Git owns durable code; worktrees are local checkouts; runtimes are host-local
sessions; dev records task intent.

## Discover what you need

Use leaf `--help` for syntax, `dev help <topic>` for workflows, and
`dev help --tree` for families. See [navigation](references/command-navigation.md)
for shortcuts and Try graduation/demotion; dashboard details: `dev help tui`.
Prefer supported JSON. Read help before mutation: some actions apply immediately,
others require preview/apply. Do not preload manuals or run routine diagnostics.

## Preserve these boundaries

- Opening needs no task. Select direct, branch or worktree deliberately; use
  explicit `--base`. Managed worktrees stay outside repositories.
- Task-free worktrees use `dev git worktree create/open`; cleanup stays reviewed.
  `dev repo list --json` supplies navigation candidates, not external preferences/history.
- `dev work start` prepares checkout/runtime; agent launch is explicit. Parallel
  writers require disjoint ownership and verified targets.
- Completion, artifacts, retirement and branch deletion are separate. Finalize
  after writer exit; retire externally. Use `retire --base` when integration is unproven.
- Cached/unknown observations, runtime `done` and merged PRs never authorize
  cleanup. Resolve guards; never improvise force removal or bypass checks.
- `dev pr checkout <URL>` is task-free; `--try` creates an independent clone.
  Provisioning is explicit; merge never cleans up locally.

## Read a reference for advanced operations

- Worktrees/lifecycle: [ownership](references/worktree-ownership.md), [lifecycle](references/task-lifecycle.md).
- Agents/prompts: [agents](references/parallel-agents.md), [handoffs](references/prompt-handoffs.md).
- History retention, exact sessions and co-commit: [artifacts](references/ai-artifacts.md).
- Cleanup: [retirement](references/agent-retirement.md), [triage](references/local-triage.md).
- Hygiene/scans/redaction: [hygiene](references/hygiene.md).
- Forks/setup/organization: [setup](references/repository-bootstrap.md), [bootstrap](references/bootstrap.md).
- SSH/fleet: [SSH](references/ssh-hosts.md).
- Dotfile setup, native chezmoi operations, or FLEET host actions: [dotfiles](references/dotfiles.md).
- Skill/MCP/instruction transfers, updates or removal: [transfers](references/agent-interop.md), [maintenance](references/skills-management.md).
- [Snippets](references/snippets.md).
- PR/MR pages, diffnav, gh-dash, checkout and merge: [pull requests](references/pull-requests.md).
- Recursive Git children: [submodules](references/submodules.md).

## Unexpected dev failures

Read [feedback and repair](references/feedback-and-repair.md). Preserve the
original task; extra investigation, repair, subagents and publication need
explicit consent covering scope and cost.

# Agent history hygiene

Preserve selected agent evidence under the repository's chosen policy. Read
`dev help ai-artifacts` and `dev artifact status` when supported: source tracking,
external archive, protection and distribution are separate choices. Commit
reviewed project knowledge; do not force-add raw history under archive/unmanaged
policy. Verify repository protection from the effective hook chain.

## Prefer the shared dev workflow

When the installed dev supports `hygiene`, use its domain for setup, scans,
private rules and reviewed text changes:

```bash
dev hygiene status
dev hygiene setup --json
dev hygiene setup --apply --plan <id> --yes
dev hygiene scan --scope staged --json
dev hygiene scan --scope history --audit --timeout 40m --json
```

`pre-commit` and `gitleaks` are needed for this repository hook recipe. An explicitly unscanned archive copy needs neither. A global `core.hooksPath` can be
correct, but its script may skip all checks when repository configs are absent.
The shared setup preserves existing hooks/comments and refuses an unverified
chain. Repository new/setup's `agent-history-hygiene` initializer uses this same
service. New default hooks block; they do not rewrite or stage files.

Per-repo secret/known/generic policy supports block/warn/off, with private local
overrides and exact reasoned exceptions. Private visibility is advice, never an
automatic exemption. SSH imports are static and reviewed: no DNS, login, Match
exec, private-key reads or rule-value export. Personal rules stay outside Git;
CI checks public rules and must state the missing personal coverage.

Read the bundled dev reference `references/hygiene.md` through `dev help hygiene`
or the public hygiene guide before rule changes or redaction. The CLI supports
all regular text, rather than treating transcripts as the only leak surface.

## Preserve the review trail

1. Identify the exact provider/session UUID from the transcript preamble. Never
   select another session just because its file is newest.
2. Commit product changes and reviewed plans. Follow the selected retention
   policy for raw history; do not broadly stage every agent directory.
3. Use `dev prepare --session provider:uuid` and finalization after its writer
   exits when that lifecycle applies. Byte stability alone is not writer proof.
4. Scan exact staged content. Partial staging must not accidentally stage
   unrelated working-copy edits.
5. In archive mode, raw history may be ignored but must be preserved before
   checkout disposal. In track mode, retain the existing exact-session workflow.
   Exclude conversation evidence from product source archives independently.

Do not close, restart or spawn agents to make hygiene checks pass without the
applicable authorization. A new agent without SpecStory does not stop an older
writer. Preserve the user's original task while offering additional cleanup.

## Reviewed redaction

```bash
dev hygiene redact --report <report-id> --file <reviewed-file> --json
# After reviewing, and after the exact artifact writer exited:
dev hygiene redact --apply --plan <plan-id> --yes --writer-stopped
```

Plans bind native file identity, contents, policy and checkout state. Stale,
modified or partial plans are not authority to overwrite current data. Keep
private recovery and rerun scans/tests after source or configuration changes.
The running transcript is left for a manual external trigger after its writer
stops. No automatic history rewrite, agent launch, commit, push or cleanup occurs.

## External archive workflow

`dev artifact setup` and `dev repo setup --artifacts` preview explicit per-repo
policy. `archive --session provider:uuid` or `--file` creates reviewed snapshots;
apply only after the exact recorder exits. Off/check/redact affect the copy,
not the live source or its index. A disabled scan is recorded as skipped.
Checked snapshots produce masked finding IDs for reasoned fixture exceptions.

Commit reviewed plans with product work before `dev prepare`. New archive intents
bind the destination and policy; redact finalization requires a reviewed
`--archive-plan`. Old tracked intents retain the compatibility scripts below.
Keep those installations while any tracked workflow still depends on them.

`artifact find` reads local committed archive records. Sync and original-backup
publication are explicit Git operations; they never transfer native session DBs.
`artifact migrate` can untrack after verified backup or build separate original,
history and filtered Git copies with commit maps. It never force-pushes source
refs. For historical exposure, use the remediation section rather than treating
path removal as a secret audit. Private raw recovery is not cache.

## Legacy scripts

The scripts remain explicit compatibility utilities. Prefer dev for new setup
and partial-staging-safe edits; a separately published remote redactor hook has
its own version and is not silently updated by dev.

- `find-session.sh --json`: locate candidate transcript/plan metadata.
- `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --dry-run`: inspect exact staging;
  without session-only it may include other dirty artifacts, so use cautiously.
- `scan-staged.sh`: masked JSON-lines locations only, never raw Match/Secret.
  Exit 0 means clean; 20 means candidate findings; legacy `--redact` selects
  exit 10 but only masks output, never modifies files. Exit 30 means missing
  gitleaks; 40 means scanner/JSON/required-parser failure; 2 means not in Git.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py --fix`: explicit legacy artifact mutation. Scanner
  failure is an error, not an empty result; console output uses full sentinels.
  This utility can restage, so use the reviewed dev flow for partial staging.
- `bootstrap-project.sh`: legacy installer; new default templates require dev
  hygiene. Its old `--migrate` targets the separately published remote redactor,
  not the new dev policy migration. Prefer `dev hygiene setup`.

SpecStory may already redact on write, but provider behavior/version is not proof
that every secret class or artifact directory is covered. Preserve existing
`[REDACTED:<rule-id>]` markers. An inert marker must never exempt another secret
on the same line. `.gitleaksignore` contains exact finding fingerprints, not
file/path globs. Portable pattern exceptions need a narrow rule/path/match scope.

## Confirmed historical exposures

Read [remediation](references/remediation.md). First distinguish fixtures,
examples and scanner candidates from confirmed credentials. Revoke/rotate a
confirmed exposed credential at its provider before considering Git history.

Shared main and immutable release tags stay unchanged in ordinary hygiene work.
Correct HEAD in a new commit, and assess old commits, tags, PR references, forks,
clones, caches and distribution artifacts separately. A force push does not erase
all copies or revoke a credential. Personal names, Git author metadata and filenames
also need an explicit impact assessment; text replacement does not rewrite them.

Never echo matching bytes or raw process arguments into a chat to investigate a
finding. Use rule IDs, safe locations and private local reports. Keep raw reports,
recovery images and personal identity dictionaries outside Git and CI logs.

## Validation

Run the skill's fixture tests for redactor/scan-wrapper changes. For dev changes,
run native hygiene/storage/text-transaction tests and the real hook test:

```bash
python scripts/test-hygiene-hooks.py --dev <absolute-built-dev>
```

It uses an isolated HOME/repository and synthetic credentials. Validate same-line
placeholder bypasses, hidden files, partial staging, missing/malformed scanner
results, writer/stale-plan refusal and private recovery. Synchronize embedded
bootstrap assets and both locales of public documentation.

5	`AGENTS.md` is the canonical repository guidance file. `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to it; edit this file rather than replacing the symlink.

7	## Toolchain and commands
8	
9	- Go 1.26.4 (from `go.mod`) builds the CLI. Python 3.11+ and `uv` are used only for the documentation site.
10	- `make` / `make all` runs `fmt -> vet -> test -> build`. `make fmt` runs `gofmt -w .` and therefore modifies files.
11	- There is no working `make lint` recipe even though `lint` appears in `.PHONY`. The repository's static gates are formatting and `go vet`.
12	
13	```bash
14	make build                         # build ./dev with git-derived version metadata
15	make test                          # go test ./...
16	go test -race -timeout 20m ./...   # CI test command
17	go test ./internal/gitx -run '^TestAddWorktreeUsesExplicitBase$'  # one test
18	go test ./internal/cli -run '^TestName/Subtest$'                  # one subtest
19	make vet                           # go vet ./...
20	files="$(gofmt -l .)" && test -z "$files"  # format check that preserves gofmt failures
21	make e2e                           # real CLI lifecycle in an isolated temporary HOME
22	make skill-sync                    # regenerate command docs, then rebuild embedded skill
23	make skill-check                   # fail when command tree and generated skill reference drift
24	make install                       # binary under PREFIX; skill in user agent directories
25	```
26	
27	Documentation uses the same sequence as CI:
28	
29	```bash
30	uv sync --frozen --extra docs
31	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source
32	uv run mkdocs build --strict
33	uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --site site
34	```
35	
36	If generated `docs/llms*.txt` files drift, regenerate them with `uv run python scripts/check-docs.py --source --generate-llms` and then rerun the documentation checks.
37	
38	## Architecture
39	
40	The executable path is deliberately shallow:
41	
42	```text
43	cmd/dev/main.go
44	  -> cli.Execute()
45	  -> cli.NewRootCommandWithIO()
46	  -> App.Load()
47	  -> Cobra command handler
48	  -> domain package(s)
49	```
50	
51	`internal/cli` assembles commands, parses flags, invokes services, and renders output. Keep policy out of command handlers; it belongs in independently testable domain packages:
52	
53	- `config` owns defaults, TOML overlays, validation, and XDG paths.
54	- `gitx` is the Git porcelain boundary and canonicalizes repository identity through the shared Git common directory.
55	- `submodule` owns versioned workspace-member intent and reversible child-clone disposal mechanisms. `gitx` supplies the local gitlink graph; `taskflow` owns recursive lifecycle policy and fresh remote-proof ordering. Gitlink checkouts are legitimate submodules, not nested managed linked worktrees.
56	- `task` persists only human intent Git cannot derive: task mode/state, owner, next action, and runtime hints. Lifecycle callers use exact-record revisions and locked compare-and-update/delete transactions rather than treating a previously read task as current.
57	- `wt` owns managed linked-worktree creation, placement, provisioning plans, and safe removal. Runtimes never create or manage Git worktrees; they surface checkout or experiment paths selected and validated by the calling `dev` flow, including managed, external, or adopted worktrees and non-Git Try directories.
58	- `runtime` abstracts Herdr, tmux, Zellij, and the no-multiplexer backend. Handles are backend-qualified hints and must be checked against live checkout coverage before reuse.
59	- `taskflow` is the UI-agnostic lifecycle authority: it separates recorded intent, typed live observations, immutable guarded plans, approvals, and partial result ledgers. Apply locks and reloads task/Git/worktree/runtime/artifact/remote identity, then rejects stale authority before mutation.
60	- `repo` discovers and deduplicates repositories; `inventory` joins repositories, Git state, tasks, all registered worktrees, and live runtime data. CLI listings and UI projections consume this joined view.
61	- `agentinterop` owns explicit MCP/skill/instruction transfer plans, guarded apply, stanza/link ownership, private recovery, and optional recipes. Native agent files and skills locks remain authoritative; only explicit preparation/check/launch paths may execute a provider or MCP server. Recovery belongs outside Git, credentials remain runtime references, and native Windows writes fail closed pending verified ACL/identity support.
62	- `triage` owns read-only cross-repository findings, clone-bound local intent, ignored-directory policy and reviewed batch ledgers; `triagetui` is its independent UI. Synchronization uses taskflow plans, and protected cleanup adds guards inside the existing repository lock and immediately before removal. Local scans never reconcile Try catalog entries.
63	- `flowtui` is an independent Bubble Tea model for the preview `dev flow` repository state-machine UI. It receives repository reads and taskflow Plan/Apply callbacks; do not embed it in or add a mode to the dashboard's `tui` model.
64	- `catalog` stores stable repository/Try identity and personal metadata. `experiment` owns Try creation, archive/restore, and graduation, including intent records and rollback/reconciliation around moves.
65	- `note` stores multiple repository thoughts as durable Markdown keyed by catalog ID and maintains a rebuildable SQLite FTS index. It is distinct from task context and the catalog's single metadata summary.
66	- `tui` owns Bubble Tea state/rendering only. `internal/cli/tui.go` injects callbacks to the same services used by non-interactive commands.
67	- `stats` is durable SQLite data; `diskusage`, note FTS, and forge/gitignore data are regenerable caches. Do not treat stats as cache.
68	- `agenthistory` owns explicit transcript/file retention policy, immutable source-bound archive copies, Git lookup/sync and isolated history migration. Archive bindings/recovery stay in private state, ordinary status never contacts remotes, and source writers/index bytes remain untouched by archiving. `artifact` keeps old commit handoffs and adds externally verified archive receipts; taskflow includes ignored capture readiness in its guarded authority.
69	- `hygiene` owns configurable secret/privacy policy, index/worktree/frozen-history scans, private identity rules and signed replacement plans. Raw findings/recovery stay outside Git; hook setup preserves foreign hooks. Large text transactions explicitly opt into configedit’s Windows backend; existing configuration flows retain their platform contracts.
70	- `feedback` owns durable private reports, sanitized public drafts, revision-bound issue/comment publication receipts and exact repair plans. CLI adapts its repair backend to the shared start flow; agent launch is explicit and prompt context never becomes a public issue body.
71	- `snippet` owns small-file share identity, account/project scope, bounded metadata/content search and frozen publication inputs. `forge` supplies GitHub/GitLab transports; CLI and REMOTE snippets share the service. Publication preserves confirmed/unknown outcomes, never retries unknown writes, and never gives snippets repository/task ownership.
72	- `forge` wraps optional `gh`, `glab`, and Azure CLI integrations and must degrade to local Git behavior when they are unavailable.
73	- `prflow` owns explicit PR/MR navigation and action authority: exact provider/head plans, task-free checkout or independent Try acquisition, private single-attempt merge receipts, and staged base synchronization through taskflow. REMOTE request pages/details are user-triggered; cached checks never authorize merge or cleanup. Unknown writes are not retried, queue/auto-merge stays native, provisioning is explicit and guarded, and gh-dash is a separate native terminal handoff.
74	- `sshhost` owns bounded static discovery of the active user OpenSSH Include closure, canonical files under `~/.ssh/dev.d`, public-key selection/generation/bootstrap, fresh authentication proofs, and the explicit handoff into dev fleet. OpenSSH and plain `ssh -G` remain semantic authority; ordinary setup/remove never rewrite foreign connection definitions, copy private keys, weaken host-key policy, or treat every alias as a fleet member. Explicit format/organize may transform selected user-owned configuration with private guarded recovery; Include restores its caller scope after each file. Named agent providers (Bitwarden, 1Password, Secretive, custom sockets) are located by stat only and never executed; selecting a named-agent key publishes only its public line and writes a v2 fragment (`IdentityAgent`, `SecurityKeyProvider`), which older binaries treat as not dev-owned, while v1 files stay byte-identical. Explicit FIDO generation binds the reviewed native tools/provider, keeps capability observations stat-only, and reports hardware created/unknown effects independently of local publication; only verified SK recovery pairs may be retained. Never use resident-key download or provider loading as a passive probe, and keep automatic Secure Enclave creation blocked until exact native identity mapping is verified.
75	- `sshflow` owns the explicit SSH/fleet/Herdr machine inventory and Plan/Apply orchestration; `herdrremote` calls the native machine CLI without writing its catalog. `configedit` owns source-bound local file transactions and private recovery outside Git, with owner leases and macOS/Linux metadata checks.
76	- `machineregistry` owns controller-local canonical machine UUIDs, scoped provider bindings, explicit unlink suppression and merge redirects in durable private SQLite. These UUIDs never replace the remote `fleet.machine_id` trust pin. `sshdiscovery` owns optional explicit Tailscale status and bounded on-link LAN observations; discovery caches are disposable and never create machine identities or prove authentication. `sshflow` joins these sources while retaining every distinct SSH connection profile; the dashboard SSH view is an adapter to the same services.
77	- `sshactivity` owns private durable per-profile usage and test observations. Usage records actual local dev-mediated SSH process starts; network/full tests never update usage. Observations retain source fingerprints and cannot authorize mutations or imply present connectivity.
78	- `tuiissue` owns typed problem guidance and reviewed native dependency installation recipes. UI actions use finite IDs and exact guarded service callbacks, never executable error text.
79	- `selfupdate` selects exact release platform assets and stages native Go source builds when an asset is absent, preferring the checksummed compact source archive over legacy Go module source. CLI owns confirmation and executable replacement; download/checksum failures never authorize a source fallback, and failed builds retain the installed binary.
80	- `platformfs` owns the native Android Termux home anchor, inherited app-data SELinux/encryption metadata recognition and no-replace publication. It also recognizes macOS kernel-managed provenance: observe it for same-file stale detection, but never restore or require it on a replacement. Verify the exact system/app prefix and all user-controlled descendants; never trust arbitrary UID-1000 directories, relabel files, chmod Android system paths or substitute an overwriting rename.
81	- `sshremote` owns strict bounded v1 SSH capability/inventory/resolve/key/connect protocols and private disposable source/route caches. Only explicit capability may initialize remote dev identity. Static inventory never evaluates SSH or agents; source profiles are scoped by observed UUID, user, root and alias. Local imports preserve native controller trust/authentication context, while remote connect reselects remote-local keys and never retries a started session.
82	- `sshcredential` owns per-context operation secrets, guarded ask/never metadata and exact provider references. System stores and explicitly selected Bitwarden contain saved passwords; the TOML ledger never does. Source-bound authentication evidence authorizes an optional save prompt, not arbitrary askpass, MFA or host-key text. Unknown provider writes stay unknown and are not retried automatically.
83	- `sshvault` owns explicit new vault-key creation, service-bound single-attempt plans, exact public receipts, and native account/profile execution context. It never imports existing private keys or writes new private material to files. Experimental Bitwarden memory creation and delegation to a native profile need separate approvals; freeze the actual environment/cwd and revalidate session/profile/tool identity without exposing session values or hashes. A session or base URL is not endpoint identity: native-context consistency and endpoint-unverified status remain separate from creation and agent visibility. Native no-interaction must prevent private JSON stdin from becoming a credential response; ambiguous writes retain receipts and never auto-retry/delete. Live vault/hardware checks remain separately consented.
84	
85	- `fleetnav` owns contextual host/repository navigation ordering, explicit Herdr profile/session selection and partial results. Repository checks precede profile changes; preparation uses a distinct versioned helper and session-scoped runtime with no focus or attach. Inside Herdr, navigation reports a native sidebar target; outside it attaches to the explicit session. Failures never implicitly switch to SSH.
86	- `fleet` merges the user-authored primary `remotes.toml` with strict dev-owned `remotes.d/ssh-<alias>.toml` registrations. Remote `dev` state remains host-local. `remote_os` selects target semantics: POSIX uses the shell launcher, while Windows uses an encoded PowerShell launcher that accepts only hidden fleet helpers, preserves sync stdin, and never applies controller path rules to remote paths.
87	
88	The principal task start flow spans `internal/cli/start.go`, `start_flow.go`, `gitx`/`wt`, `runtime`, and `task`: resolve the canonical repository and explicit base, create or select the checkout, provision/open it, then persist and annotate the task. Task-backed park/resume/completion/retirement and exact unmanaged Adopt/Remove policy belong in `taskflow`; CLI commands, the dashboard, `sweep`, and `flowtui` are adapters. Preserve report-before-apply and no-data-loss ordering, including the isolated compatibility paths that have not migrated to taskflow.
89	
90	State is split intentionally:
91	
92	- Git remotes/branches are durable code truth.
93	- Worktrees are disposable local checkouts.
94	- Runtime sessions are per-host and re-derivable.
95	- Task TOML and catalog assets hold only intent/identity that Git cannot answer.
96	- Repository quick-note Markdown is durable sidecar data; `notes.db` is only its disposable search index.
97	- `stats.db` is durable observation data; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/*` is disposable.
98	- SSH source/route caches are disposable; remote dev UUIDs, local canonical machine UUIDs and fleet trust pins are separate identities. Credential policy/reference TOML is durable intent; its provider-owned secret is not a cache. Removing a reference does not erase a vault item or revoke a remote password.
99	- The user's OpenSSH configuration is durable connection truth. Ordinary setup/remove own only the exact top-level `Include ~/.ssh/dev.d/*.conf` and structurally valid fragments in `~/.ssh/dev.d`; key bootstrap sends public material only and has no private-key transfer or remote-key revocation lifecycle.
100	- Fleet intent is the merged primary `remotes.toml` plus generated sibling `remotes.d` fragments. A generated fragment exists only after explicit `dev ssh setup --fleet` / `--to fleet|both` or `dev ssh manage --action register --to fleet|both`, and a fresh ordinary alias login; controller caches and each remote machine's paths/tasks/runtime remain re-derivable or host-local.
101	- `paths.state_dir/machines/registry.db` is durable controller-local identity and binding intent; `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dev/ssh-discovery/` contains disposable dated Tailscale/LAN observations. Plain `dev ssh list` stays static; `--tailscale` explicitly queries the optional local CLI and `--lan` reads cached observations. Neither list nor dashboard refresh scans the LAN. The active SSH dashboard may refresh local Tailscale status when `[tui.ssh].background_refresh` is enabled; native discovery returns typed observations independently of cache writes. Candidate setup preserves source/scope provenance and per-stage retained effects.
102	
103	## Behavioral contracts
104	
105	- Task modes are `worktree`, `branch`, and `direct`; lifecycle states are `hot`, `warm`, `cold`, and `done`. READY/REVIEW/MERGED/RETIRED are action readiness or result milestones, never extra persisted states.
106	- Persisted intent, observed facts, and guarded action plans are separate layers. Unknown, failed, skipped, loading, or stale observations never become a false clean/closed fact.
107	- Use an explicit base for branch/worktree creation. Do not infer a safe base from whichever branch happens to be checked out.
108	- Never nest a managed worktree inside a repository. Removing a worktree does not remove its branch, and dirty removal stays opt-in.
109	- Cold parking requires committed, pushed, reconstructible work before runtime/worktree cleanup.
110	- Submodule initialization uses committed gitlinks, never implicitly advances to `main`. Whole child-clone disposal requires explicit recursive approval and fresh recovery proof for its private refs/objects; outer and shared canonical repositories are retained. Local graph refresh never performs remote proof. Child task/runtime/artifact claims block parent disposal.
111	- A taskflow Plan is bound to the exact task revision and repository/worktree/ref/runtime/artifact identities shown at Plan time. Apply must lock, reload, and revalidate those identities; a changed revision or authority produces a stale-plan result with no new effect.
112	- Managed rows receive only legal mode/state lifecycle actions. An unmanaged linked checkout may be adopted by metadata-only task creation or removed only when exact, clean, unclaimed, non-harness, and branch-preserving; canonical, harness-owned, ambiguous/conflicting, locked, prunable, or incompletely observed rows fail closed for destructive actions.
113	- Local repository refresh must not contact remotes. Fetching refs and querying a forge are explicit network actions, and review evidence is run-local manual evidence limited to portable existence/state/draft/URL/provider/time fields; never infer review decisions or checks.
114	- Reconciliation flows such as `sweep`, command-level `adopt`, and bootstrap organization plans report before applying changes. Direct actions such as `wt rm`, `tries archive`, and `cache clear` mutate immediately after their own safety checks; do not treat them as previews. `dev flow` is plan-first regardless of the adapted command's normal CLI interaction.
115	- Raw Git and configured external tools remain outside dev-mediated locks, revalidation, and safety guarantees. Existing expert CLI flags remain compatibility surface even when the preview flow deliberately omits them.
116	- A recognized agent in a canonical checkout occupies it regardless of whether its status is working, idle, done, or unknown. Shared-writer overrides require coordinated disjoint ownership.
117	- A parallel launch target is only the exact root pane returned for a newly created first-class Herdr worktree; reused/fallback/unverified surfaces fail closed.
118	- `dev ls --json` is an external automation contract. Add fields rather than renaming/removing existing fields; apply the same compatibility care to other documented structured output, including `dev hygiene report --json` (`hygiene_summary` schema 1). Stored summaries are historical observations, not proof of current source bytes.
119	- Quick notes attach to the canonical repository through catalog identity. Markdown is durable, note deletion requires confirmation, and clearing/rebuilding note FTS must never delete source files.
120	- Explicit SSH format/organize and fleet profile rename/remove are plan-first exceptions for user-selected files; retain comments, Include order, original metadata and private recovery. Never activate dormant files with a new broad Include. Herdr machine add may prepare/start a remote server; leave native approvals native, and remove/disable never stops remote sessions.
121	- SSH initialization is report-before-apply; managed host changes are confined to canonical dev-owned fragments. Full bootstrap requires an explicit existing key or explicit generation, registers fleet only when explicitly selected, and reports interrupted remote installation as unknown rather than pretending to roll it back.
122	- SSH wizard permission preflight may separately review and apply metadata-only tightening on exact current-user-owned canonical/selected paths. It never recursively chmods, changes ownership, guesses ACLs, or widens permissions; completed repairs survive later cancellation. Listing and dry-run never repair permissions. Local key listing evaluates OpenSSH only behind explicit `--alias`; selected key material remains service-bound and is revalidated before configuration changes and bootstrap.
123	- `dev ssh key doctor` exposes the same permission Plan/Apply with bounded metadata-only key discovery; `--key` restricts the reviewed scope, and `--fix` requires a complete safe plan plus confirmation. Default doctor never mutates, reads private contents, or queries agents/remotes. Batch repairs revalidate the whole reviewed union and retain successful tightening on partial failure.
124	- Source-aware SSH setup can use `--auth existing` without installing a key, and registers only explicitly selected `--to fleet|herdr|both` destinations. Tailscale SSH advertisement is advisory; its port-22 endpoint is not an authorized_keys bootstrap target. Preserve the key-authentication guard and never treat Tailscale policy login as proof that a selected public key worked. Names, ports and cached observations never authorize machine merges; binding/source changes invalidate reviewed plans.
125	- Fleet-source SSH discovery selects explicit hosts without recursive fleet traversal. Local ProxyJump imports never copy remote identity/agent/trust paths; cached route data cannot authorize apply. `connect --on` is one interactive fixed-helper session with no agent forwarding or arbitrary command payload. Normal SSH errors retain child exit status.
126	- Controller password brokerage uses a private per-operation Unix socket or protected Windows pipe, never password argv/environment/files. Exact host/user/port/route contexts gate replies and save evidence. Remote source-to-target credentials remain outside this feature; native key/passphrase interaction is separate.
127	- Filesystem transitions must retain path traversal/symlink, same-filesystem, source revalidation, and rollback/reconciliation checks.
128	
129	## Versioning and changelog
130	
131	The current published baseline is `v0.3.3` (2026-09-25). The CLI version authority is an immutable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag:
132	
133	- `Makefile` derives development builds with `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty` and injects `internal/cli.Version` through `-ldflags`. The `--match` filter is load-bearing: any other tag in the repository (a `backup/` or `rescue/` marker, say) must never become `--version`.
134	- `go install ...@version` recovers the module version from Go build information.
135	- `pyproject.toml` version `0.0.0` belongs only to the MkDocs environment and is not the CLI version.
136	
137	Every user-visible feature must be added to `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` as part of the feature change. Do not publish or describe a feature build under an older release's version; a release containing new compatible behavior must receive a newer version. Decide from public compatibility impact rather than blindly from the commit type.
138	
139	**When to release.** A tag is not an occasional ceremony; it is how a downstream binary learns it is stale. `go install ...@latest` resolves to the newest tag, so anything merged but untagged is invisible outside this repository.
140	
141	- A landed branch that stands alone is released immediately: bump the patch during `0.x` (`v0.1.x`) and tag it as the last step of landing.
142	- A landed branch belonging to an announced milestone accumulates in `[Unreleased]`; the milestone closes with a minor bump (`v0.2.0`).
143	- Never let `[Unreleased]` grow past one milestone's worth of work. `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.11` were tagged retroactively on 2026-08-29 precisely because 38 commits accumulated with no release.
144	
145	**What downstream gets.** Every release from `v0.2.0` forward publishes platform binaries and `SHA256SUMS` alongside the GitHub release, and `dev doctor` reports the running version so a user can compare without leaving the terminal. A release that ships neither leaves `dev --version` as the only signal, which is what the freshness work exists to fix.
146	
147	For a release:
148	
149	1. Move the relevant `[Unreleased]` entries into `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` and update comparison links.
150	2. Update version-pinned install examples when the documented recommended release changes.
151	3. Push `main` first. `release.yml` asserts the tagged commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, so a tag pushed ahead of its branch fails validation.
152	4. Tag the exact commit on `main` as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`; never move or reuse a published tag. Never push `backup/*` or `rescue/*` tags — a tag reachable from a commit that predates the `--match` filter breaks the workflow's `./dev --version` assertion.
153	5. Let `.github/workflows/release.yml` run CI, verify `./dev --version`, build the platform matrix, create the GitHub release, and update Scoop. The `daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap` repository is the single Homebrew formula writer: its hourly/manual sync validates the published assets and installs/tests the formula before committing. This repository does not need a Homebrew tap-writing token.
154	
155	To retry Homebrew synchronization, run `gh workflow run sync.yml --repo daviddwlee84/homebrew-tap -f tool=dev-cli`. This uses the tap repository’s own token and does not create or move an application tag. Stable formulas install release binaries; `brew install --HEAD daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli` retains the source-build path.
156	
157	Stable release tags only are accepted by the current workflow; prerelease tags are not supported.
158	
159	## Keep implementation, skill, and docs aligned
160	
161	`internal/skill/dev-cli/` is shipped product surface, not incidental prose: `internal/skill/skill.go` embeds the entire tree in the binary. A code change is incomplete when the bundled skill or public documentation still describes old behavior.
162	
163	| Change | Required synchronization |
164	|---|---|
165	| Cobra command name, `Use`, `Short`, flag, or global option | Run `make skill-sync`, inspect `internal/skill/dev-cli/references/commands.md`, then run `make skill-check`. Never edit the generated block by hand. |
166	| Task modes/states/defaults or lifecycle preconditions | Update `SKILL.md`, `references/task-lifecycle.md`, README, embedded help, relevant English and zh-TW workflow/mental-model/compatibility pages, and transition tests. |
167	| Worktree placement, provisioning, include rules, strategies, or safety checks | Update `references/worktree-ownership.md`, README/public worktree docs, config examples, and focused `wt` tests. |
168	| Runtime protocol, fallback order, activation, agent collision, exact-pane launch, or cleanup behavior | Update `references/runtime-herdr.md`, `references/parallel-agents.md`, compatibility docs, and runtime/lifecycle tests. Keep the boundary clear: `dev start` prepares a checkout/runtime surface; it does not launch an agent. |
169	| Bootstrap scan/layout/index/move behavior | Update `references/bootstrap.md`, public bootstrap docs, and bootstrap tests. |
170	| Config fields/defaults or structured output | Update generated command help where applicable, authored reference pages and both locales, examples, and compatibility tests. |
171	| Quick-note storage, identity, search, structured output, or TUI behavior | Update README, embedded help, `SKILL.md`, `references/notes.md`, and paired English/zh-TW mental-model, workflow, TUI, commands/config, compatibility, and freshness pages. |
172	| Any user-visible feature or fix | Update `CHANGELOG.md`; update README/help/MkDocs/skill wherever they make the affected claim. |
173	
174	`make skill-check` proves only that generated command syntax matches the Cobra tree. It cannot detect drift in lifecycle semantics, JSON schemas, safety claims, examples, README, embedded help, or authored skill references; review those manually. Because the skill is compiled with `go:embed`, rebuild after any skill edit before testing the bundled output.
175	
176	English and zh-TW MkDocs pages are maintained as a pair. Run the strict documentation checks above after changing either locale, navigation, snippets, or freshness metadata.
177	
178	## Hygiene and skill batch operations
179	
180	`internal/hygiene` owns per-repository setup plans and batch ledgers. REPOS and
181	`hygiene manage` are adapters; JSON batch management previews only. Keep legacy
182	artifact finalizers until their independent lifecycle is replaced. Cached machine
183	privacy imports use only bounded local cache readers and revalidate their source.
184	`internal/agentskill` owns selected-removal policy: exact native names/agent scopes
185	or bundled manifests, source/ownership/dependency proof and postconditions under
186	the provider lease. The complete native Windows suite and dedicated native gates
187	are required. Keep unsupported mutation boundaries explicit and test their native
188	rejections; do not restore continue-on-error or skip supported behavior to hide
189	portability failures. Historical advisory step conclusions were not proof of a
190	passing suite.
191	
192	Windows CI discovers every Go package and shards the large CLI/taskflow root
193	tests, examples and fuzz seeds across eight native runners. The required audit
194	rejects incomplete coverage and failed or timed-out invocations. Keep discovery,
195	execution and audit tied to the same commit and toolchain; preserve logs for
196	each invocation. Linux/macOS retain the monolithic race suite. After changing
197	the runner, run `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p test_windows_shards.py`.
198	
199	## Agent history policy
200	
201	`dev help ai-artifacts` separates source retention, archive location, protection
202	and distribution. New configuration is opt-in. Sources are SpecStory Markdown or
203	explicit files; provider IDs name the originating agent. Do not infer writer exit
204	from byte stability or close agents to finalize evidence. Archive mode verifies
205	ignored bytes before cleanup; existing tracked intents retain their original lane.
206	`git-filter-repo` only operates on new verified copies. Ordinary migration never
207	rewrites source refs or published tags, and raw backups are not secret audits.
208	
209	`artifact` owns native intent revisions, exact transcript selection and writer
210	Guard/CAS checks. Product-first remains the default (committed products, empty
211	index). Explicit co-commit binds a feature-only index to a separately installed
212	canonical v2 helper and authentic wrapper launched without `--allow-commit`.
213	Native code never launches/closes the agent or invents queue acknowledgement,
214	SessionEnd or export evidence. Queue success, including queued-but-not-bound,
215	requires reporting finalization queued and exiting without more repository work.
216	External finalization uses canonical prepare-only, fresh native guards and exact
217	helper revision before one commit-capable call; uncertain outcomes reconcile
218	only. Commit proof includes parent, tree, full normalized message and unique
219	request identity, not trailers alone. Status/readiness keep native intent and
220	helper observations separate and never mutate or reconcile. Helper/tool identity
221	drift, unsupported versions and native Windows fail closed; no automatic install
222	or v1-journal upgrade. Per-finding noncredential review releases only the exact
223	sanitized run's rotation gate, never restores secrets or bypasses hooks; actual
224	credentials still require rotation and unknown findings remain blocked.
225	
226	## Distribution verification
227	
228	Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p test_distribution.py` and, after
229	committing packaging edits, `python3 scripts/check-distribution.py --version v0.3.3`.
230	The latter validates independent source and Go module payloads, including their
231	embedded resources. Evidence-only nested `go.mod` files intentionally remove
232	those directories from the parent module ZIP; do not run module tidy in them.

```text
1	# Evaluate unified REPOS and FLEET browsing
2	
3	Status: research — P? · M
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	FLEET's host tree makes SSH, Herdr saved-machine controls and remote repository
8	inventory available in one place. Showing all local repositories there also
9	duplicates REPOS, which already has richer Git/worktree/task/notes actions.
10	The current decision is to hide the local FLEET host by default. The `a` key and
11	action menu can reveal it at the end of the host list for the current session.
12	
13	## Question to answer
14	
15	Would a shared host/repository browser make navigation simpler, or would it
16	obscure the distinction between a local working checkout and a remote observation?
17	Evaluate shared projections or a host selector before committing to a single
18	dashboard view. Retaining separate views is an acceptable outcome.
19	
20	## Constraints and tradeoffs
21	
22	- Keep the fast local startup and reuse the accepted REPOS snapshot. A unified
23	  browser must not rescan local repositories or wait for remote SSH.
24	- Preserve local Git/worktree/task/notes actions and exact checkout identities;
25	  a cached remote row is not permission to execute a local action.
26	- Keep each host's loading, error, cache age and authentication independent.
27	  Search must state which hosts are covered and avoid implicit extra connections.
28	- Herdr registration/enabled state belongs to the executing host's client
29	  catalog. It is distinct from repository state and live remote sessions.
30	- Keep repository actions, host connection actions and saved-machine management
31	  recognizable without duplicating every menu in both views.
32	- Preserve keyboard navigation, selection on refresh, and explicit local/remote
33	  path semantics. CLI fleet JSON and existing host-local state remain compatible.
34	
35	## Before implementation
36	
37	Compare three representative workflows: local-only work, opening a known remote
38	repository, and searching for a repository across several partially available
39	hosts. Prototype the smallest shared projection or host switcher, then assess
40	whether it reduces navigation while retaining clear action ownership. Do not
41	couple this research to the shipped Herdr enable/disable/remove controls.
42
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
23	type tuiFuture[T any] struct {
24		ready chan struct{}
25		value T

29	func startTUIFuture[T any](work func() (T, error)) *tuiFuture[T] {
30		future := &tuiFuture[T]{ready: make(chan struct{})}
31		go func() {
32			future.value, future.err = work()
33			close(future.ready)
34		}()
35		return future
36	}

39		select {
40		case <-ctx.Done():
41			var zero T
42			return zero, ctx.Err()
43		case <-f.ready:
44			return f.value, f.err
45		}
46	}

297		if live.runtime != nil {
298			name = live.runtime.Name()
299		}
300		row.Context = inventory.WithRuntime(row.Context, name, live.sessions, live.err)
301		row.Live = false
302		row.RuntimeHandle = ""
303		row.RuntimeStatus = ""
304		row.Runtime = name
305		if sessions := row.Context.Sessions(); len(sessions) > 0 {
306			row.Live = true
307			row.RuntimeHandle = sessions[0].Handle
308			row.RuntimeStatus = sessions[0].AgentStatus
309		}
310	}
```

```text
10	// LocalLoadRequest identifies the three view generations sharing one source
11	// snapshot. Each result remains independently replaceable.
12	type LocalLoadRequest struct {
13		CycleGeneration uint64
14		TasksGeneration uint64
15		ReposGeneration uint64
16		TriesGeneration uint64
17		ShowAllTries    bool
18		ForceSizes      bool
19	}
20	
21	// LocalResult is one terminal TASKS, REPOS, or TRY snapshot.
22	type LocalResult struct {
23		Phase      string
24		View       View
25		Generation uint64
26		Tasks      []inventory.Row
27		Repos      []RepoRow
28		Tries      []TryRow
29		Valid      bool
30		Err        error
31	}
32	
33	// LocalLoad is a cancellable stream owned by the caller's context.
34	type LocalLoad struct {
35		ID      uint64
36		Request LocalLoadRequest
37		Results <-chan LocalResult
38	}
39	
40	// LocalActions starts one shared local source cycle.
41	type LocalActions struct {
42		Start func(context.Context, LocalLoadRequest) LocalLoad
43	}
44	
45	type localMsg struct {
46		load   LocalLoad
47		result LocalResult
48		done   bool
49	}
50	
51	func (m Model) startLocalLoad() tea.Cmd {
52		if m.actions.Local.Start == nil {
53			return nil
54		}
55		request := LocalLoadRequest{
56			CycleGeneration: m.localGeneration,
57			TasksGeneration: m.viewLoad(ViewTasks).generation,
58			ReposGeneration: m.viewLoad(ViewRepos).generation,
59			TriesGeneration: m.viewLoad(ViewTries).generation,
60			ShowAllTries:    m.showAllTries,
61			ForceSizes:      m.forceSizeReload,
62		}
63		load := m.actions.Local.Start(m.localReadContext(), request)
64		load.Request = request
65		if load.ID == 0 || load.Results == nil {
66			return nil
67		}
68		return waitForLocal(load)
69	}
70	
71	func waitForLocal(load LocalLoad) tea.Cmd {
72		return func() tea.Msg {
73			result, ok := <-load.Results
74			if !ok {
75				return localMsg{load: load, done: true}
76			}
77			return localMsg{load: load, result: result}
78		}
79	}
80	
81	func (m Model) applyLocalResult(result LocalResult) (Model, bool) {
82		accepted := false
83		if result.View == ViewRepos && result.Phase != "" {
84			return m.applyRepoProgress(result)
85		}
86		token := m.currentToken()
87		path := m.repoFocusPath()
88		switch result.View {
89		case ViewTasks:
90			accepted = m.applyViewResult(
91				ViewTasks, result.Generation, result.Valid, "live", resultFreshness(result.Err),
92				len(result.Tasks), result.Err, result.Valid,
93			)
94			if accepted && result.Valid {
95				m.rows = append([]inventory.Row(nil), result.Tasks...)
96			}
97		case ViewRepos:
98			accepted = m.applyViewResult(
99				ViewRepos, result.Generation, result.Valid, "live", resultFreshness(result.Err),
100				len(result.Repos), result.Err, result.Valid,
101			)
102			if accepted && result.Valid {
103				m.setViewStatus(ViewRepos, "")
104				m.acceptCompleteRepoSnapshot(result.Err)
105				if result.Err != nil {
106					m.repos = mergeRepoProgress(m.repos, result.Repos)
107				} else {
108					m.repos = completeRepoRows(m.repos, result.Repos)
109				}
110				m.repoProgressPhase = 3
111				m.matchRemoteLocals()
112			}
113		case ViewTries:
114			accepted = m.applyViewResult(
115				ViewTries, result.Generation, result.Valid, "live", resultFreshness(result.Err),
116				len(result.Tries), result.Err, result.Valid,
117			)
118			if accepted && result.Valid {
119				m.tries = append([]TryRow(nil), result.Tries...)
120				m.matchRemoteLocals()
121			}
122		}
123		m.restoreRepoFocus(token, path)
124		m.setAt(m.at())
125		return m, accepted
126	}
```

```text
101			cancel()
102		}
103		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(m.baseContext())
104		m.loadContexts[index] = ctx

108			// Cancellation must always follow the generation that can complete it.

112		state.generation++

115		state.loading = true

185		state := &m.loads[int(view)]
186		state.hasSnapshot = true
187		state.source = source
188		state.freshness = freshness
189		state.outcome = perftrace.OutcomeSuccess
190		state.actionable = actionable
191	}
192	
193	func (m *Model) applyCacheSeed(view View, generation uint64, rows int, freshness perftrace.Freshness) bool {
194		state := &m.loads[int(view)]
195		if generation != state.generation {
196			m.trace.Mark(perftrace.TUIViewResultDiscarded, perftrace.Fields{
197				View: view.traceView(), Stage: perftrace.StageDiscarded,
198				Generation: generation, Outcome: perftrace.OutcomeSuperseded,
199			})
200			return false
201		}
202		m.seedViewSnapshot(view, perftrace.SourceCache, freshness, true)
203		count := rows
204		m.trace.Mark(perftrace.TUIViewSnapshotAccepted, perftrace.Fields{
205			View: view.traceView(), Stage: perftrace.StageCacheAccepted,
206			Source: perftrace.SourceCache, Freshness: freshness,
207			Outcome: perftrace.OutcomeSuccess, Generation: generation, Rows: &count,
208		})
209		return true
210	}
211	
212	// applyViewResult accepts only the current request generation. valid says the
213	// producer returned a real snapshot; it is independent of slice nil-ness so a
214	// successful empty result can replace older rows.
215	func (m *Model) applyViewResult(view View, generation uint64, valid bool, source perftrace.Source,
216		freshness perftrace.Freshness, rows int, err error, actionable bool) bool {
217	
218		state := &m.loads[int(view)]
219		if generation != state.generation {
220			m.trace.Mark(perftrace.TUIViewResultDiscarded, perftrace.Fields{
221				View: view.traceView(), Stage: perftrace.StageDiscarded,
222				Generation: generation, Outcome: perftrace.OutcomeSuperseded,
223			})
224			return false
225		}
226	
227		state.loading = false
228		outcome := resultOutcome(valid, err)
229		state.outcome = outcome
230		if valid {
231			state.hasSnapshot = true
232			state.source = source
233			state.freshness = freshness
234			state.actionable = actionable
235			count := rows
236			m.trace.Mark(perftrace.TUIViewSnapshotAccepted, perftrace.Fields{
237				View: view.traceView(), Stage: perftrace.StageSnapshotAccepted,
238				Source: source, Freshness: freshness, Outcome: outcome,
239				Generation: generation, Rows: &count,
240			})
241		} else if state.hasSnapshot {
242			state.freshness = perftrace.FreshnessStale
243		}
244		m.viewErrors[int(view)] = err
245		m.trace.Mark(perftrace.TUIViewLoadFinished, perftrace.Fields{
246			View: view.traceView(), Stage: perftrace.StageFinished,
247			Source: state.source, Freshness: state.freshness, Outcome: outcome,
248			Generation: generation,
249		})
250		if cancel := m.loadCancels[int(view)]; cancel != nil {
251			cancel()
252			m.loadCancels[int(view)] = nil
253			m.loadContexts[int(view)] = nil
254		}
255		return true
256	}
257	
258	func resultFreshness(err error) perftrace.Freshness {
259		if err != nil {
260			return perftrace.FreshnessStale
261		}
262		return perftrace.FreshnessFresh
263	}
264	
265	func resultOutcome(valid bool, err error) perftrace.Outcome {
266		switch {
267		case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled):
268			return perftrace.OutcomeCanceled
269		case err != nil && valid:
270			return perftrace.OutcomePartial
271		case err != nil || !valid:
272			return perftrace.OutcomeFailed
273		default:
274			return perftrace.OutcomeSuccess
275		}
276	}
277	
278	func (m Model) viewLoad(view View) viewLoadState { return m.loads[int(view)] }

281		state := m.viewLoad(view)
282		if state.loading {
283			return false
284		}
285		if state.hasSnapshot && state.freshness == perftrace.FreshnessFresh {
286			return false
287		}
288		return !state.hasSnapshot || state.freshness == perftrace.FreshnessStale || state.outcome == perftrace.OutcomeFailed
289	}
```

```text
1	package cli

3	import (

8		"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/agenttarget"

11	)
12	
13	func resolverOutcome(err error) perftrace.Outcome {
14		if err != nil {
15			return perftrace.OutcomeFailed
16		}
17		return perftrace.OutcomeSuccess
18	}
19	
20	// tuiRuntimeResolver moves runtime auto-detection off the first-view path while
21	// sharing exactly one result across inventory loads and actions.
22	type tuiRuntimeResolver struct {
23		trace   *perftrace.Recorder
24		resolve func() runtime.Runtime
25		once    sync.Once
26		ready   chan struct{}
27		rt      runtime.Runtime
28	}
29	
30	func newTUIRuntimeResolver(app *App) *tuiRuntimeResolver {
31		snapshot := *app
32		return &tuiRuntimeResolver{
33			trace: app.trace, resolve: snapshot.Runtime, ready: make(chan struct{}),
34		}
35	}
36	
37	func (r *tuiRuntimeResolver) Resolve(ctx context.Context) (runtime.Runtime, error) {
38		r.once.Do(func() {
39			go func() {
40				finish := r.trace.Start(perftrace.TUIRuntimeResolve, perftrace.Fields{})
41				r.rt = r.resolve()
42				finish(perftrace.OutcomeSuccess)
43				close(r.ready)
44			}()
45		})
46		if ctx == nil {
47			ctx = context.Background()
48		}
49		select {
50		case <-ctx.Done():
51			return nil, ctx.Err()
52		case <-r.ready:
53			return r.rt, nil
54		}
55	}
56	
57	// tuiProjectRootResolver keeps startup-context discovery lazy and shared by
58	// SKILLS/MCP reads and skill actions.
59	type tuiProjectRootResolver struct {
60		trace   *perftrace.Recorder
61		ctx     context.Context
62		getwd   func() (string, error)
63		resolve func(context.Context, string) (agenttarget.Target, error)
64		once    sync.Once
65		ready   chan struct{}
66		target  agenttarget.Target
67		err     error
68	}
69	
70	func newTUIProjectRootResolver(trace *perftrace.Recorder, ctx context.Context) *tuiProjectRootResolver {
71		if ctx == nil {
72			ctx = context.Background()
73		}
74		cwd, cwdErr := os.Getwd()
75		return &tuiProjectRootResolver{
76			trace: trace, ctx: ctx, getwd: func() (string, error) { return cwd, cwdErr }, resolve: agenttarget.Current,
77			ready: make(chan struct{}),
78		}
79	}
80	
81	func (r *tuiProjectRootResolver) ResolveTarget(ctx context.Context) (agenttarget.Target, error) {
82		r.once.Do(func() {
83			go func() {
84				finish := r.trace.Start(perftrace.TUIProjectRootResolve, perftrace.Fields{})
85				cwd, err := r.getwd()
86				if err == nil {
87					r.target, err = r.resolve(r.ctx, cwd)
88				}
89				r.err = err
90				finish(resolverOutcome(err))
91				close(r.ready)
92			}()
93		})
94		if ctx == nil {
95			ctx = context.Background()
96		}
97		select {
98		case <-ctx.Done():
99			return agenttarget.Target{}, ctx.Err()
100		case <-r.ready:
101			return r.target, r.err
102		}
103	}
104	
105	func (r *tuiProjectRootResolver) Resolve(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
106		target, err := r.ResolveTarget(ctx)
107		return target.CheckoutRoot, err
108	}
109	
110	func (r *tuiProjectRootResolver) Current() (string, bool) {
111		select {
112		case <-r.ready:
113			return r.target.CheckoutRoot, r.err == nil
114		default:
115			return "", false
116		}
117	}
```

```text
302	func runTUI(app *App) error {
303		app.traceTUI = true
304		runCtx, cancelRun := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
305		defer cancelRun()
306		finishSetup := app.trace.Start(perftrace.TUISetup, perftrace.Fields{})
307		// --color, NO_COLOR and TERM=dumb governed every other surface but stopped
308		// at the dashboard, which resolved its own palette independently.
309		tui.SetColorEnabled(app.outStyle().enabled)
310		appState := newTUIAppState(app)
311		runtimeResolver := newTUIRuntimeResolver(app)
312		projectRootResolver := newTUIProjectRootResolver(app.trace, runCtx)
313		localLoader := newTUILocalLoader(app, runtimeResolver)
314		localLoader.current = appState.Current
315		fleetBackend := newTUIFleetBackend(appState.Current)
316	
317		reload := func(ctx context.Context) ([]inventory.Row, error) {
318			rt, err := runtimeResolver.Resolve(ctx)
319			if err != nil {
320				return nil, err
321			}
322			tasks, err := appState.Current().Tasks.List()
323			if err != nil {
324				return nil, err
325			}
326			return inventory.Collect(ctx, tasks, rt, inventory.Options{}), nil
327		}
328		reloadRepos := func(ctx context.Context) ([]tui.RepoRow, error) {
329			rt, err := runtimeResolver.Resolve(ctx)
330			if err != nil {
331				return nil, err
332			}
333			// Keep Try repositories in the model's local snapshot so cached REMOTE
334			// rows can be matched and cleared correctly. The REPOS view filters them.
335			return collectReposWithOptions(ctx, appState.Current(), rt, repoCollectOptions{IncludeTries: true})
336		}
337		reloadRemote := func(ctx context.Context, locals []tui.RepoRow) ([]tui.RemoteRow, error) {
338			return collectRemotesForRows(ctx, appState.Current(), locals)
339		}
340		capabilityTargets := func(ctx context.Context, locals []tui.RepoRow, scope tui.CapabilityScope) ([]agenttarget.Target, error) {
341			current, err := projectRootResolver.ResolveTarget(ctx)
342			if err != nil {
343				return nil, err
344			}
345			return tuiCapabilityTargets(locals, current, scope), nil
346		}
347		reloadSkills := func(ctx context.Context, locals []tui.RepoRow, scope tui.CapabilityScope) ([]agentskill.Skill, error) {
348			targets, err := capabilityTargets(ctx, locals, scope)
349			if err != nil {
350				return nil, err
351			}
352			result, err := inventory.CollectAgentSkills(ctx, targets, inventory.AgentSkillOptions{})
353			if err != nil {
```

```text
8	func mergeRepoProgress(previous, updates []RepoRow) []RepoRow {
9		rows := append([]RepoRow(nil), previous...)
10		for _, row := range updates {
11			found := false
12			for i, old := range rows {
13				if old.Repo.Path == row.Repo.Path {
14					if row.Pending == "loading" && old.Pending != "loading" {
15						found = true
16						break
17					}
18					if row.TopologyPending && !old.TopologyPending && old.Pending == "" {
19						row.Topology, row.TopologyErr, row.TopologyPending = old.Topology, old.TopologyErr, false
20					}
21					if row.Usage == nil {
22						row.Usage, row.SizeError = old.Usage, old.SizeError
23					}
24					rows[i] = row
25					found = true
26					break
27				}
28			}
29			if !found {
30				rows = append(rows, row)
31			}
32		}
33		return rows
34	}
35	
36	func (m Model) applyRepoProgress(result LocalResult) (Model, bool) {
37		state := m.viewLoad(ViewRepos)
38		if result.Generation != state.generation || m.repoProgressPhase == 3 {
39			return m, false
40		}
41		phase := 1
42		if result.Phase != "cache" {
43			phase = 2
44		}
45		if phase < m.repoProgressPhase {
46			return m, false
47		}
48		m.repoProgressPhase = phase
49		token := m.currentToken()
50		path := m.repoFocusPath()
51		m.repos = mergeRepoProgress(m.repos, result.Repos)
52		m.loads[int(ViewRepos)].hasSnapshot = true
53		m.loads[int(ViewRepos)].freshness = perftrace.FreshnessStale
54		m.loads[int(ViewRepos)].actionable = false
55		m.loads[int(ViewRepos)].source = perftrace.SourceLive
56		if phase == 1 {
57			m.loads[int(ViewRepos)].source = perftrace.SourceCache
58		}
59		count := len(m.repos)
60		m.trace.Mark(perftrace.TUIViewSnapshotAccepted, perftrace.Fields{View: perftrace.ViewRepos, Stage: perftrace.StageFirstEnrichment, Source: m.loads[int(ViewRepos)].source, Freshness: perftrace.FreshnessStale, Generation: result.Generation, Rows: &count})
61		message := fmt.Sprintf("Refreshing local repositories… %d visible", count)
62		if phase == 1 && len(result.Repos) > 0 {
63			message = "Cached " + result.Repos[0].ObservedAt.Local().Format("Jan 2 15:04") + " · " + message
64		}
65		m.setViewStatus(ViewRepos, message)
66		m.restoreRepoFocus(token, path)
67		m.setAt(m.at())
68		return m, true
69	}
70	
71	func (m Model) repoFocusPath() string {
72		if item, ok := m.currentRepoItem(); ok {
73			if checkout, child := item.checkout(); child {
74				return checkout.Worktree.Path
75			}
76			return item.Repo.Repo.Path
77		}
78		return ""
79	}
80	func (m *Model) restoreRepoFocus(token selectionToken, path string) {
81		if m.selectToken(token) || m.view != ViewRepos || path == "" {
82			return
83		}
84		for i, item := range m.visibleRepoItems() {
85			candidate := item.Repo.Repo.Path
86			if checkout, child := item.checkout(); child {
87				candidate = checkout.Worktree.Path
88			}
89			if candidate == path {
90				m.setAt(i)
91				return
92			}
93		}
94	}
95	
96	func completeRepoRows(previous, rows []RepoRow) []RepoRow {
97		merged := mergeRepoProgress(previous, rows)
98		out := make([]RepoRow, 0, len(rows))
99		for _, row := range rows {
100			for _, candidate := range merged {
101				if row.Repo.Path == candidate.Repo.Path {
102					out = append(out, candidate)
103					break
104				}
105			}
106		}
107		return out
108	}
109
```

```text
387		m.overlay = menu
388		if m.view != ViewFleet {
389			m.err = nil
390		}
391		return m
392	}

394	func (m Model) runOverlayAction() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
395		if m.overlay.optionCount == 0 || m.overlay.optionIndex >= m.overlay.optionCount {
396			return m, nil
397		}
398		action := m.overlay.options[m.overlay.optionIndex].action
399		option := m.overlay.options[m.overlay.optionIndex]
400		if option.disabled != "" {
401			m.status, m.overlay.body, m.overlay.scroll = option.disabled, option.disabled, 0
402			return m, nil
403		}
404		if issueAction(action) {
405			return m.dispatchAction(option)
406		}
407		if option.fleetProfile != "" {
408			return m.openFleetProfile(m.overlay.fleetHost, option.fleetProfile)
409		}
410		if option.fleetID != "" {
411			host := m.overlay.fleetHost
412			m.overlay = overlayState{}
413			return m.runFleetHostActionFor(host, option.fleetID)
414		}
415		token := m.overlay.selection
416		spec, registered := findAction(m.view, action)
417		if !registered {
418			return m.dispatchAction(option)
419		}
420		if spec.Scope == actionSelection && (!m.selectToken(token) || (token.revision != "" && m.currentToken().revision != token.revision)) {
421			m.overlay = overlayState{}
422			m.err = fmt.Errorf("selected row changed while its action menu was open")
423			return m, nil
424		}
425		availability := spec.availability(m.actionContext())
426		if !availability.Applicable {
427			m.overlay = overlayState{}
428			m.err = fmt.Errorf("selected action is no longer applicable; reopen actions")
429			return m, nil
430		}
431		if availability.Reason != "" {
432			return m.dispatchAction(option)
433		}
434		if action == listActionFleetProfiles {
435			return m.openFleetProfiles()
436		}
437		m.overlay = overlayState{}
438		if option.tool != "" {
439			return m, m.launchTool(option.tool)
440		}
441		if option.column != "" {
442			return m.cycleTableSort(option.column)
443		}
444		return m.dispatchAction(option)
445	}

746	func (m Model) toggleSelectedRepo() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
747		item, ok := m.currentRepoItem()
748		if !ok || item.Repo.Worktrees == 0 {
749			return m, nil
750		}
751		if item.Repo.Context.WorktreeErr != nil {
752			m.err = item.Repo.Context.WorktreeErr
753			return m, nil
754		}
755		if item.child() {
756			for i := m.repoCursor - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
757				if !m.visibleRepoItems()[i].child() {
758					m.repoCursor = i
759					break
760				}
761			}
762		}
763		m.toggleRepo(item.Repo)
764		return m, nil
765	}

767	func (m Model) promptSelectedRemoteClone() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
768		row, ok := m.currentRemote()
769		if !ok || row.Cloned() {
770			return m, nil
771		}
772		if row.CloneProblemPath != "" {
773			if _, err := os.Lstat(row.CloneProblemPath); err == nil {
774				m.err = fmt.Errorf("inspect or move the existing clone destination at %s before retrying", config.Contract(row.CloneProblemPath))
775				return m, nil
776			}
777			m.setRemoteCloneProblem(row, "")
778		}
779		if !m.reposReadyForClone() {
780			m.setViewStatus(ViewRemote, "wait for local repositories to finish loading")
781			return m, nil
782		}
783		m.remoteClonePrompt = row
784		return m.prompt(modeConfirmClone, row.Repo.FullName, "enter clone; o clone and open; esc cancel")
785	}

805	func (m Model) openSelectedCapabilityFile() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
806		path, err := m.capabilityFilePath()
807		if err != nil {
808			m.err = err
809			return m, nil
810		}
811		if m.actions.EditFile == nil {
812			m.err = fmt.Errorf("opening capability files is unavailable")
813			return m, nil
814		}
815		edit, err := m.actions.EditFile(path)
816		if err != nil {
817			m.err = err
818			return m, nil
819		}
820		if edit.Command == nil {
821			m.err = fmt.Errorf("capability editor returned no process")
822			return m, nil
823		}
824		view := m.view
825		m.status = "editing " + config.Contract(path) + "…"
826		return m, runExecProcess(edit.Command, func(runErr error) tea.Msg {
827			if edit.Complete != nil {
828				runErr = edit.Complete(runErr)
829			}
830			return capabilityFileEditedMsg{view: view, err: runErr}
831		})
832	}

834	func (m Model) runTryListAction(action listAction) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
835		row, ok := m.currentTry()
836		if !ok {
837			return m, nil
838		}
839		var tryAction TryAction
840		switch action {
841		case listActionTryMark:
842			tryAction = TryMark
843		case listActionTryDeprecate:
844			tryAction = TryDeprecate
845		case listActionTryReactivate:
846			tryAction = TryReactivate
847		case listActionTryArchive:
848			tryAction = TryArchive
849		case listActionTryRestore:
850			tryAction = TryRestore
851		}
852		switch tryAction {
853		case TryMark, TryRestore:
854			return m.openTryForm(tryAction, row)
855		case TryArchive:
856			return m.openTryConfirmation(tryAction, row)
857		case TryDeprecate, TryReactivate:
858			m.status = string(tryAction) + " in progress…"
859			return m, m.applyTry(TryRequest{Action: tryAction, ID: row.reference()})
860		default:
861			return m, nil
862		}
863	}
```

```markdown
# REPOS favorites and fast navigation

## Context

使用者常透過 `dev → 2 (REPOS) → / 搜尋名稱 → Enter` 在 Herdr 開啟日常開發的 repository，但選中目標後仍需等待掃描。希望能收藏常用 repo、置頂，並優先更新。這是兩個相連但獨立的需求：可預期的常用項目排序，以及不被全域掃描阻擋的單一 repo 導航。

本輪只研究與規劃，不修改產品程式，也不操作實際 repo/runtime。

## Proposed scope (pending code-path verification)

- 手動 favorite，以穩定 repository identity 儲存為個人 intent；不以使用頻率自動改寫收藏。
- REPOS 收藏置頂、可辨識標記，以及能在列表內切換收藏的操作。
- 優先更新收藏 repo，同時保持其他 repo 的正常發現及背景更新。
- 導航只依賴所選目標的必要即時驗證，不等全域完整掃描；快取狀態不可冒充 fresh facts 或授權 cleanup。
- 不延伸到遠端 FLEET 收藏、task ownership、agent launch、雲端同步或自動使用頻率排名。

## Investigation

- 正在確認 REPOS 載入／排序／搜尋／Enter／Herdr handoff 的實作與測試。
- 現有 `backlog/repos-fleet-unification.md` 已要求保留快速 local startup、沿用接受的 REPOS snapshot，且不得因遠端或重掃描阻塞 local browsing；本功能保持 REPOS 的 local scope，不併入 REPOS/FLEET 整合研究。

## Verification

待定位實作後補齊 focused tests、隔離 HOME 的真實 TUI 重現，以及 skill/雙語 docs 同步檢查。
```

```text
207		spec, ok := findAction(m.view, option.action)
208		if !ok {
209			m.err = fmt.Errorf("action %d is not registered for %s", option.action, m.view)
210			return m, nil
211		}
212		a := spec.availability(m.actionContext())
213		if !a.Applicable {
214			return m, nil
215		}
216		reason := a.Reason
217		if reason == "" {
218			reason = option.disabled
219		}
220		if reason != "" {
221			m.status = reason
222			if m.viewLoad(m.view).loading {
223				m.setViewStatus(m.view, reason)
224			}
225			if m.overlay.kind == overlayActionMenu {
226				m.overlay.body = reason
227				m.overlay.scroll = 0
228			}
229			return m, nil
230		}
231		return spec.Run(m, option)
232	}

273		}
```

```text
10	// openCheckout makes a directory live, asking the backend to treat it as a git
11	// worktree when it knows how — that is what groups the checkout under its
12	// parent repo in a sidebar instead of listing it as an unrelated directory.
13	func openCheckout(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, dir, label string) (runtime.OpenResult, error) {
14		if wo, ok := rt.(runtime.WorktreeOpener); ok {
15			return wo.OpenWorktree(ctx, dir, label)

17		return rt.Open(ctx, dir, label)

20	// activateRuntime performs the interactive half of navigation. Runtime Open
21	// calls are detached by design; explicit open/resume actions opt into either
22	// switching the current multiplexer client or attaching from a plain shell.
23	func activateRuntime(ctx context.Context, rt runtime.Runtime, handle string) error {
24		if rt == nil || rt.Name() == "none" || handle == "" {
25			return nil
26		}
27		activator, ok := rt.(runtime.Activator)
28		if !ok {
29			return errors.New("runtime " + rt.Name() + " cannot activate sessions")
30		}
31		return activator.Activate(ctx, handle)
```

```text
314	// Open implements Runtime. An already-open directory is reused rather than
315	// opened twice. It remains detached; explicit navigation calls Activate.
316	func (h *Herdr) Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error) {
317		existing, err := h.List(ctx)
318		if err != nil {
319			return OpenResult{}, err
320		}
321		for _, s := range existing {
322			if s.Covers(dir) {
323				return OpenResult{Handle: s.Handle, Surface: "workspace", Opened: true}, nil
324			}
325		}
326		return h.createWorkspace(ctx, dir, label)
327	}
328	
329	// OpenExternalCoordinator always creates a fresh workspace. Destructive
330	// cleanup cannot run in a reused or caller-owned surface.
331	func (h *Herdr) OpenExternalCoordinator(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error) {
332		return h.createWorkspace(ctx, dir, label)
333	}
334	
335	func (h *Herdr) createWorkspace(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error) {
336		args := []string{"workspace", "create", "--cwd", dir, "--no-focus"}
337		if label != "" {
338			args = append(args, "--label", label)
339		}
340		var res struct {
341			Workspace herdrWorkspace `json:"workspace"`
342			RootPane  herdrPane      `json:"root_pane"`
343		}
344		if err := h.call(ctx, &res, args...); err != nil {
345			return OpenResult{}, err
346		}
347		if res.Workspace.WorkspaceID == "" {
348			return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("herdr workspace create: response has no workspace id")
349		}
350		if res.RootPane.PaneID == "" || res.RootPane.WorkspaceID != res.Workspace.WorkspaceID {
351			return OpenResult{}, h.rejectCreatedWorkspace(ctx, res.Workspace.WorkspaceID,
352				"herdr workspace create: response has no correlated root pane")
353		}
354		return OpenResult{
355			Handle: res.Workspace.WorkspaceID, Surface: "workspace", Opened: true,
356			Created: true, RootPaneID: res.RootPane.PaneID,
357		}, nil
358	}
359	
360	// Activate focuses a workspace and then mirrors hhere's client behavior:
361	// inside Herdr the existing client switches immediately; outside Herdr a new
362	// client attaches after the caller has left any alternate-screen UI.
363	func (h *Herdr) Activate(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
364		if handle == "" {
365			return nil
366		}
367		if err := h.Focus(ctx, handle); err != nil {
368			return err
369		}
370		if os.Getenv("HERDR_ENV") != "" {
371			return nil
372		}
373		return runInteractive(ctx, h.bin)
374	}
375	
376	// Focus selects a workspace on the ordinary local adapter. Session-scoped
377	// remote preparation forbids this server-wide operation; its caller must use
378	// an explicit native client activation capability separately.
379	func (h *Herdr) Focus(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
380		if h.session != "" {
381			return errors.New("scoped remote preparation cannot change server-wide client focus")
382		}
383		if handle == "" {
384			return nil
385		}
386		return h.call(ctx, nil, "workspace", "focus", handle)
387	}

389	// OpenWorktree implements WorktreeOpener: it registers an already-created git
390	// worktree as a herdr workspace, which is what makes the checkout appear in
391	// the sidebar grouped under its parent repo with its own branch and
392	// ahead/behind row.
393	func (h *Herdr) OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (OpenResult, error) {
394		args := []string{"worktree", "open"}
395		if source := h.parentWorktreeSource(ctx, path); source != "" {
396			// Pin the canonical parent checkout instead of relying on the calling
397			// pane. This preserves native nested grouping even when dev is invoked
398			// from a different Herdr workspace.
399			args = append(args, "--cwd", source)
400		} else if h.session != "" {
401			return OpenResult{}, errors.New("cannot resolve an explicit parent checkout for scoped Herdr preparation")
402		}
403		args = append(args, "--path", path, "--no-focus")
404		if label != "" {
405			args = append(args, "--label", label)
406		}
407		var res struct {
408			Workspace   herdrWorkspace `json:"workspace"`
409			Worktree    herdrWorktree  `json:"worktree"`
410			RootPane    herdrPane      `json:"root_pane"`
411			AlreadyOpen *bool          `json:"already_open"`
412		}
413		if err := h.call(ctx, &res, args...); err != nil {
414			if h.session != "" {
415				return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("scoped Herdr worktree open failed; any partial workspace is retained for inspection: %w", err)
416			}
417			// Fall back to a plain workspace: the checkout being visible matters
418			// more than it being tagged with git provenance. A fallback root pane is
419			// withheld so callers cannot mistake it for a first-class worktree target.
420			fallback, fallbackErr := h.Open(ctx, path, label)
421			fallback.RootPaneID = ""
422			fallback.Surface = "workspace"
423			return fallback, fallbackErr
424		}
425		handle := res.Workspace.WorkspaceID
426		if handle == "" {
427			handle = res.Worktree.OpenWorkspaceID
428		}
429		if handle == "" {
430			return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("herdr worktree open: response has no workspace id")
431		}
432		if res.AlreadyOpen == nil {
433			// Without this protocol field, the handle may belong to a reused
434			// workspace. Do not close it or expose its pane as newly created.
435			return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("herdr worktree open: response does not say whether the workspace was reused")
436		}
437		created := !*res.AlreadyOpen
438		if created && (res.RootPane.PaneID == "" || res.RootPane.WorkspaceID != handle) {
439			return OpenResult{}, h.rejectCreatedWorkspace(ctx, handle,
440				"herdr worktree open: new workspace response has no correlated root pane")
441		}
442		rootPaneID := ""
443		if created {
444			rootPaneID = res.RootPane.PaneID
445		}
446		return OpenResult{
447			Handle: handle, Surface: "worktree", Opened: true,
448			Created: created, RootPaneID: rootPaneID,
449		}, nil
450	}
451	
452	func (h *Herdr) rejectCreatedWorkspace(ctx context.Context, handle, reason string) error {
453		if h.session != "" {
454			return fmt.Errorf("%s; retained incomplete workspace %s in Herdr session %s for inspection", reason, handle, h.session)
455		}
456		if err := h.Close(ctx, handle); err != nil {
457			return fmt.Errorf("%s; could not close incomplete workspace %s: %w", reason, handle, err)
458		}
459		return fmt.Errorf("%s; closed incomplete workspace %s", reason, handle)
```
